reason: E1 only describes test methods for CoCrFeNi-based alloys and provides no evidence on Ti doping or oxide glaze formation. E2 demonstrates reactive wear protection via an amorphous-crystalline oxide nanocomposite in a different alloy system (TiNbZr-Ag), but the hypothesis extrapolates this mechanism to CoCrFeNi with Ti without direct evidence that Ti doping in CoCrFeNi produces a similar adaptive nanocrystalline oxide layer or reduces friction/wear across the full temperature range. The key premises thus lack specific prior support.
premises: Ti dopant in CoCrFeNi will oxidize during sliding to form a continuous nanocrystalline oxide layer
The in-situ oxide layer will act as an adaptive lubricating glaze from RT to 800 °C
The oxide layer will reduce direct metal-to-metal contact and accommodate plastic deformation
Ti-doped CoCrFeNi will show lower friction and wear than undoped CoCrFeNi across the full temperature range
The 'reactive wear protection' mechanism demonstrated in (TiNbZr)75Ag25 applies to CoCrFeNi with Ti doping
